reason: I'll start with the outer barrier: the lipids fill gaps between skin cells, which seems useful for holding water in.
expectation: I expect a more protective outer skin layer, though I don't know exactly how complete it will be.

alternatives.reason: The coil and duct clearly make a sweat outlet, but I want to build the barrier first.
The vessels fit the deeper supporting tissue, another useful part to build afterward.

effect: The outer cells and lipids slow water loss rather than stopping it completely. I can now build the deeper living layer.
reaction: The reduced water arrows made the barrier's job clear.
reason: I'll add blood vessels to the supporting tissue before joining it to the surface.
expectation: I expect supporting skin tissue with vessels running through it.

alternatives.reason: This would join the surface to the supporting tissue, but I want to add its vessels first.
The sweat outlet is also a goal, but I'll continue building the skin layers first.

effect: The deeper tissue supplies the outer layer's living cells even though vessels do not enter that layer. I can join the two layers now.
reaction: That supply connection was useful to see.
reason: I'll join the deeper skin to the protective surface to build the skin layers.
expectation: I expect a combined skin layer with the water-resistant surface above the supplied living tissue.

alternatives.reason: The sweat outlet is also needed, but I'll finish joining the layers first.

effect: The protective and living layers are joined, with spaces for a sweat outlet and nerve endings.
reaction: The outlined spaces make the next steps clear.
reason: I'll connect the sweat gland to its duct to make the outlet named in the goal.
expectation: I expect a sweat gland with a route to a skin pore, ready to fit into the layered skin.

alternatives.reason: The nerve endings also fit the skin, but I'll make the sweat outlet first.

effect: The gland and duct now form a route to a pore, ready to fit into the skin.
reaction: The outlet works as expected; nothing surprising.
reason: I'll fit the completed sweat outlet into its named slot in the layered skin.
expectation: I expect the gland to sit beneath the surface with its duct reaching a pore, while the sensory-endings slot remains open.

alternatives.reason: The nerve endings also need fitting, but I'll finish the sweat route first.

effect: The sweat gland and duct are fitted into the layered skin; the sensory endings are still needed.
reason: I'll add the nerve endings to the remaining slot; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the nerve endings to sit at different depths in the skin, completing its listed parts.

effect: The skin now has its sweat outlet and nerve endings, so it is ready to connect to the body.
reaction: The separate structures make skin's different jobs clearer.
reason: I'll connect the completed skin to the body; it's the only offered combination and matches the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the layered skin to cover the body, with its vessels, gland and nerve endings included.

effect: The completed skin connects to the body's vessels and nerves. The final views also show how it responds to warmth and cold while still limiting water loss.
reaction: It was interesting that the same surface can resist water loss and let sweat out through pores.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the completed skin to the body was most worthwhile: the warm and cold views brought its protection, sweat, blood vessels and nerves together.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the already-made sweat gland into its named slot felt predictable, though it was clear why it belonged there.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the outer layer has no blood vessels and its living cells get supplies from the tissue underneath.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary. The named slots and pictures explained where the parts belonged, although the compatible-pair menu supplied the pairings.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter: seeing separate parts come together in the final body model was interesting, though some fittings were predictable.
